question: Can one language-model agent transmit token-aligned last-layer hidden states, or a much shorter learned latent recurrence, to a separately trained actor so that the pair solves interactive and symbolic tasks more accurately or quickly than matched text communication?

key_findings.claim: Interlat's full-length channel sends the sender's last-layer state from every autoregressive message position through a learned receiver-side adapter.
key_findings.evidence: For a generated completion y_1:L, the sender collects h_l immediately before predicting each y_l, producing H in R^(Lxd). Boundary tokens surround H in the actor input, and a lightweight self-attention plus projection adapter rescales and interprets the foreign states before the actor generates its response.

key_findings.claim: The actor is explicitly trained to depend on task-matched latents while remaining behaviorally aligned with the corresponding language plan.
key_findings.evidence: The actor objective combines task cross-entropy, a distribution-separation term comparing matched and cross-task latent messages, and KL/cosine alignment to predictions conditioned on the source model's text plan. A curriculum samples a prefix replacement rate from 0 to 1 and mixes plan-token embeddings with later latent states, gradually exposing the actor to the all-latent channel.

key_findings.claim: The displayed separation-loss equation is inconsistent with both the prose and the reported training curve.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 3 defines L_sep as negative mean Jensen-Shannon divergence, so identical conditional distributions have loss 0 and maximally separated distributions approach -ln(2). Figure 3 instead says a plateau near positive ln(2) means no separation and a later drop means successful use. That interpretation corresponds to ln(2)-JS or a classification loss, not the printed -JS expression; the prose also alternates between minimizing and maximizing separation.

anchors.section: Figure 3 and Semantics and Learning Dynamics

key_findings.claim: A second model learns short latent messages against a frozen actor through task, behavioral-agreement, and geometry losses.
key_findings.evidence: The compression model autoregressively feeds its own last hidden state back as the next input embedding for K latent steps without token decoding. The frozen actor supplies teacher-forced task loss; entropy-weighted KL matches the actor's full-latent behavior where full latents reduce uncertainty; and cosine alignment matches mean actor-side latent directions after length resampling.

key_findings.claim: Full-length latent communication improves ALFWorld success over text and no-communication controls for the two Qwen actors, but the LLaMA advantage over full CoT is negligible on unseen tasks.
key_findings.evidence: For Qwen2.5-7B, Interlat reports 70.48% seen/65.42% unseen versus Text 64.29/62.44, CoT-full 67.14/64.93, and No-Comm 62.14/62.19. For Qwen2.5-0.5B it reports 61.19/57.46 versus CoT-full 57.86/50.75. For LLaMA3.1-8B it reports 70.71/70.90 versus CoT-full 69.35/70.82, only a 0.08-point unseen difference.

key_findings.claim: Cross-task and component ablations show that the trained actor uses instance-specific channel content, while also showing heavy dependence on the curriculum and adapter.
key_findings.evidence: On Qwen2.5-7B, replacing the message with another task's latents lowers 70.48/65.42 seen/unseen success to 61.43/61.94. Removing the latent curriculum yields 33.10/20.65; removing separation gives 58.81/60.70; removing alignment gives 56.90/53.98; and removing the adapter nearly collapses success to 4.05/4.48.

key_findings.claim: The heterogeneous-model experiment establishes trainable channel compatibility, not zero-shot model-agnostic semantics.
key_findings.evidence: A LLaMA actor is trained to consume Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct states through Interlat and reaches 70.95% seen/71.39% unseen, versus the same-family LLaMA Interlat result 70.71/70.90. The adapter and actor are trained on that source channel, no unadapted transfer is tested, and the small gain has no reported significance test; sender quality is also changed along with model family.

key_findings.claim: MATH is a mixed negative result: Interlat loses to CoT overall and only slightly leads on the hardest reported level.
key_findings.evidence: Interlat reports 36.88% overall accuracy versus 38.35% for CoT-full. It trails on Level 3 (40.08 versus 45.65) and Level 4 (27.45 versus 31.19) but reaches 15.80 on Level 5 versus 15.05 for CoT-full. No sample counts, uncertainty, or significance test is attached to the 0.75-point Level-5 difference.

key_findings.claim: The up-to-24x efficiency claim changes the sender, message length, and quality target, and measures message generation rather than full agent inference.
key_findings.evidence: The quoted ratio is 9.19 seconds for a full Qwen-Instruct message versus 0.39 seconds for an 8-step untrained short message; the trained 8-step model is separately reported at 0.20 seconds. The corresponding full success is 70.48/65.42 seen/unseen, versus 64.00/57.46 for untrained 8-step and 66.43/60.45 for trained 8-step. Table 3 calls the measure end-to-end latency of the message generation process, excluding the receiver's episode execution and communication bytes.

key_findings.claim: Compression preserves useful performance over a broad length range, but every most-compressed trained model remains below its own full-latent endpoint.
key_findings.evidence: On Qwen, trained K=128/64/32/16/8 gives seen success 68.10/67.14/66.90/66.43/66.43 and unseen 62.94/61.94/61.94/61.69/60.45, versus full 70.48/65.42. On LLaMA, trained K=8 gives 64.32/64.89 versus full 70.71/70.90. Thus the bottleneck is useful and fast but not lossless in task behavior.

key_findings.claim: Training-free truncation yields a useful negative result against simple monotonic compression assumptions.
key_findings.evidence: For Qwen, retaining 50% of a full message raises seen success from 70.48 to 72.14 but lowers unseen success from 65.42 to 61.19; other ratios vary non-monotonically. This suggests temporal redundancy and possible regularization, but selecting the best of many ratios without a held-out selection protocol cannot establish that 50% is intrinsically optimal.

key_findings.claim: The output-distribution and PCA analyses do not directly demonstrate that latent messages contain or preserve parallel reasoning hypotheses.
key_findings.evidence: The paper interprets broader top-k next-token probability support and lower P50(S10) as persistent parallelism, but these observables can also reflect uncertainty, entropy, or calibration and are not linked to decoded alternative plans or counterfactual branches. PCA clusters mean-pooled states by task template, but the underlying prompts already identify task type; no text-state control, label permutation, variance-explained report, or causal direction intervention is shown.

anchors.section: Figure 5 and Why compression is effective

key_findings.claim: The full-length method is latent at the interface but not entirely language-free in sender computation.
key_findings.evidence: Its transmitted H is defined from the last states produced immediately before each token of an autoregressively generated completion, and the corresponding text plan is used during actor training. Only the separately trained compression model performs its message-generation loop wholly through recurrent latent embeddings; the final actor still decodes textual actions or answers.

key_findings.claim: The three-agent study shows feasibility beyond a pair, but its incremental gains are small and lack uncertainty.
key_findings.evidence: On Qwen2.5-0.5B, latent chain-3/tree-3 achieve 62.14/59.44 and 62.85/60.77 seen/unseen, compared with latent chain-2 at 61.19/57.46. Matched text chain-3/tree-3 reach 58.34/51.89 and 61.19/56.75. The table reports neither run-to-run variation nor a compute/parameter match for the extra learned merge projection.

key_findings.claim: The paper evaluates semantic utility but not the physical bandwidth, memory footprint, or safety observability of transmitting dense hidden-state tensors.
key_findings.evidence: Full messages contain L by d floating-point states rather than L token IDs, yet no bytes transferred, quantization, inter-device bandwidth, peak memory, adapter FLOPs, or distributed-system latency is reported. The limitations and ethics sections explicitly acknowledge that latent messages are not human-readable and could bypass language-based safety mechanisms.

method.core_idea: Replace the text passed from a reasoning agent to an actor with the reasoning model's token-aligned last-layer hidden-state trajectory, train the actor to interpret that trajectory, and optionally train a second reasoning model to generate a short latent-only trajectory that preserves the frozen actor's behavior.
method.mechanism: A sender first generates a plan and exposes the pre-token hidden state at every completion position. The receiver wraps those states in boundary tokens, passes them through self-attention and projection, and is full-parameter fine-tuned using task loss, matched-versus-mismatched distribution separation, plan-conditioned behavior alignment, and a stochastic text-prefix-to-latent curriculum. For compression, the actor and adapter freeze while a base reasoning model repeatedly feeds its own projected last state back as the next embedding; task cross-entropy, uncertainty-weighted KL to full-latent behavior, and cosine alignment of actor-side mean latent directions supervise K-step messages.
assumptions: Token-aligned last-layer hidden states contain task-relevant information not adequately conveyed by the corresponding decoded plan.
A learned adapter and actor can identify that information rather than memorizing sender-specific coordinate or prompt shortcuts.
Cross-task messages sampled within a batch are valid negatives and do not make the separation objective solvable from superficial length or template cues.
Behavioral alignment to a language plan stabilizes training without constraining the latent channel to reproduce only information already present in text.
A prefix curriculum from token embeddings to hidden states transfers to the all-latent test condition.
A frozen actor is an adequate judge of which full-message information should survive compression.
Entropy reduction relative to a no-latent actor identifies informative output positions rather than overconfidence or calibration artifacts.
Cosine alignment of mean actor-side features preserves useful geometry despite temporal resampling.
ALFWorld success and MATH accuracy capture collaborative reasoning rather than teacher quality, actor fine-tuning budget, or trajectory-distribution differences.
Three runs and a 5% validation split are sufficient for selecting checkpoints and numerous compression ratios, despite the lack of reported significance tests.
Message-generation latency on one machine is representative of end-to-end multi-agent efficiency even though transmission bytes and actor execution are omitted.
Open access to internal hidden states and trainable receiver parameters is available.

techniques.role: Transmits the sender's last-layer pre-token state sequence directly instead of decoded token IDs.
Uses lightweight self-attention and projection to rescale, contextualize, and dimension-match a foreign latent trajectory.
Pushes actor output distributions under correct and cross-task messages apart so the actor cannot ignore the channel.
Regularizes latent-conditioned actor logits toward those elicited by the corresponding language plan.
Replaces a randomly sized prefix of latent positions with aligned token embeddings during training to stabilize the all-latent receiver.
Generates K compressed message states by projecting and feeding the reasoning model's last hidden state back as its next embedding.
Trains compressed latents to reproduce full-latent actor distributions specifically at positions where the full message reduces uncertainty.
Penalizes cosine drift between mean actor-side features induced by compressed and resampled full messages.
Tests cross-task replacement, covariance-shaped noise, Gaussian surrogates, and covariance-preserving rotations for channel sensitivity.
Projects parallel Explorer and Critic trajectories into one actor input for a three-agent tree topology.

evaluations.setting: ALFWorld official seen/unseen tasks with 20-step episode cap, Qwen2.5-7B actor, three runs
evaluations.metric: Task success rate and mean steps on successful/all trials
evaluations.result: Interlat obtains 70.48% seen and 65.42% unseen success with 9.41/12.54 and 9.86/13.37 steps.

evaluations.setting: ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-0.5B and LLaMA3.1-8B actors
evaluations.result: Interlat reports 61.19/57.46 on Qwen-0.5B and 70.71/70.90 on LLaMA-8B.
evaluations.baseline: CoT-full reports 57.86/50.75 and 69.35/70.82 respectively; the LLaMA unseen difference is 0.08 point.

evaluations.setting: Cross-family Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct sender to trained LLaMA3.1-8B actor
evaluations.result: 70.95% seen and 71.39% unseen, demonstrating that a learned adapter can bridge the pair.
evaluations.baseline: Same-family LLaMA Interlat is 70.71/70.90; no zero-shot or frozen-adapter transfer baseline is reported.

evaluations.result: Interlat is 36.88 overall, 40.08 Level 3, 27.45 Level 4, and 15.80 Level 5.
evaluations.baseline: CoT-full is 38.35 overall, 45.65 Level 3, 31.19 Level 4, and 15.05 Level 5.

evaluations.metric: Seen/unseen success rate over three runs
evaluations.result: Without curriculum 33.10/20.65; without separation 58.81/60.70; without alignment 56.90/53.98; without adapter 4.05/4.48.

evaluations.setting: Qwen compression from full message to K in {128,64,32,16,8}
evaluations.metric: ALFWorld seen/unseen success and sender message-generation latency
evaluations.result: Trained K=8 reaches 66.43/60.45 in 0.20 seconds; trained K=128 reaches 68.10/62.94 in 2.25 seconds.
evaluations.baseline: Full Qwen-Instruct message reaches 70.48/65.42 in 9.19 seconds; untrained K=8 reaches 64.00/57.46 in 0.39 seconds.

evaluations.setting: LLaMA compression from full message to K in {128,64,32,16,8}
evaluations.metric: ALFWorld seen/unseen success and sender message-generation latency
evaluations.result: Trained K=8 reaches 64.32/64.89 in 0.24 seconds; trained K=128 reaches 66.46/66.35 in 2.80 seconds.
evaluations.baseline: Full LLaMA-Instruct message reaches 70.71/70.90 in 10.20 seconds.

evaluations.setting: Qwen2.5-0.5B two- and three-agent chain/tree topologies

evaluations.metric: ALFWorld success, top-k probability support, PCA template clusters, and adapter centroid shifts
evaluations.result: Cross-task and several distribution-destroying perturbations reduce success; trained compressed states retain broader top-k output support, and 3,119 mean-pooled states cluster by task template.
evaluations.baseline: Matched original messages, untrained/base-model compression states, and pre-adapter PCA states; no causal branch-decoding or task-label control is provided.

limitations: Author-stated: evaluation centers on a controlled sender-actor setting, one embodied benchmark, and one symbolic benchmark rather than dynamic roles, long-horizon collaboration, tools, retrieval, or external memory.
Author-stated: the channel requires internal hidden-state access and therefore excludes closed/API-only models.
Author-stated: dense latent messages are not human-readable, complicating debugging, monitoring, and failure analysis.
Author-stated: latent communication could bypass language-based safety mechanisms; PCA and output probabilities are only preliminary transparency tools.
Reviewer-identified: full-length communication still requires autoregressive generation of the aligned language trajectory at the sender.
Reviewer-identified: the paper reports message-generation time but not bytes transferred, inter-device bandwidth, memory, adapter cost, or full episode latency.
Reviewer-identified: many reported gains are small relative to the stated three-run variability and no significance testing is provided.
Reviewer-identified: cross-family results train the receiver on that sender and therefore do not demonstrate a universal or zero-shot shared latent language.
Reviewer-identified: output entropy and PCA clustering do not identify semantic content or parallel reasoning paths without stronger causal controls.
Reviewer-identified: the separation objective's printed sign and Figure 3 scale do not agree, obstructing exact replication.
failure_modes: Without the token-to-latent curriculum, the actor's latent comprehension becomes unstable and unseen ALFWorld success falls to 20.65%.
Without the learned adapter, raw foreign states are effectively unusable and success collapses to about 4%.
Aggressive compression drops Qwen success by about 4-5 points and LLaMA success by about 6 points relative to full messages.
A receiver can learn coordinate conventions specific to one sender, model family, task-template distribution, or adapter rather than transferable semantics.
Cross-task negatives may permit template or trajectory-length shortcuts if negative construction is not matched on superficial properties.
Dense full-length tensors can cost more network bandwidth and memory than text even when sender decoding latency is lower downstream.
Latent-only channels can hide unsafe plans or coordination failures from token-level monitors and human auditors.
Output-distribution broadness can represent indecision or poor calibration rather than productive hypothesis diversity.
A frozen actor can teach the compressor to preserve that actor's idiosyncratic behavior while discarding information useful to a different downstream agent.
The method cannot operate when hidden states are unavailable, encrypted, dimensionally incompatible without adaptation, or produced by models whose internal basis drifts after updates.
reusable_insights: Matched-versus-mismatched message interventions are a practical test that a receiver uses communication content rather than merely benefiting from extra parameters.
A token-to-latent curriculum can bridge a severe representation-distribution shift for receivers trained to consume continuous internal states.
Behavioral distillation through a frozen downstream model avoids requiring one-to-one reconstruction between full and compressed latent trajectories.
Uncertainty-weighted distillation can focus compression on output positions where side information changes the downstream prediction.
Separate full-channel utility from compression utility: a representation may improve task success yet still require a learned bottleneck for system-level efficiency.
Cross-family compatibility should be decomposed into sender quality, trainable adapter capacity, zero-shot transfer, and post-adaptation performance.
Communication evaluations should report accuracy, sender compute, receiver compute, transmitted bytes, network latency, memory, and observability together.
open_questions: Does Interlat still outperform text when sender and receiver compute, trainable parameters, teacher plans, and transmitted byte budgets are exactly matched?
Can a frozen adapter trained on one sender transfer zero-shot to another model, checkpoint, tokenizer, or hidden-state basis?
What objective was actually implemented for separation: -JS, ln(2)-JS, a discriminator loss, or another normalized quantity?
Can decoded counterfactual branches or environment interventions validate the claimed preservation of parallel hypotheses?
How does performance change under bandwidth quantization, lossy transmission, packet delay, or multi-device deployment?
Can a compressor trained against one frozen actor preserve information for multiple actors or future tasks?
Do the Level-5 MATH and three-agent gains survive larger samples, preregistered comparisons, and statistical correction?
How can latent messages be monitored, edited, attributed, and safety-filtered without decoding them back into language?
What is the scaling law in agent count, message rounds, latent length, hidden dimension, and adapter capacity?
Can the method work with truly latent sender computation from the start rather than hidden states coupled to a generated language plan?

competitive_landscape.title: Communicating Activations Between Language Model Agents
competitive_landscape.difference: Ramesh and Li fuse one model's intermediate activation into another model mid-forward-pass with zero additional parameters or data and report compute savings. Interlat instead sends a whole token-aligned last-layer trajectory through a trained adapter and actor, then adds learned latent-only compression.

competitive_landscape.title: Let Models Speak Ciphers: Multiagent Debate through Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: CIPHER communicates the expectation of output embeddings over the vocabulary and needs no model-weight modification, preserving belief information beyond a sampled token. Interlat communicates internal last-layer states rather than output-distribution embeddings and trains explicit interpretation and compression modules.

competitive_landscape.title: Augmenting Multi-Agent Communication with State Delta Trajectory
competitive_landscape.difference: State Delta Encoding transmits natural-language tokens plus token-wise changes in hidden state, retaining interpretability while enriching the channel. Interlat removes transmitted text and uses absolute final-layer states, trading observability for a pure latent interface and learned compression.

competitive_landscape.title: Cache-to-Cache: Direct Semantic Communication Between Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: C2C projects and gates a source model's KV cache into selected target layers, avoiding intermediate text and reporting end-to-end latency gains. Interlat inserts last-layer message states as an input prefix and compresses them through a separate recurrent latent generator; it does not compare against cache fusion.

competitive_landscape.title: Thought Communication in Multiagent Collaboration
competitive_landscape.difference: Thought Communication uses a latent-variable identifiability framework to extract shared and private thoughts and route them among agents, with theoretical recovery guarantees. Interlat transmits raw token-aligned hidden states and relies on supervised behavior to learn their meaning, without identifying shared factors.

competitive_landscape.title: Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems
competitive_landscape.difference: LatentMAS postdates Interlat's first submission and offers a training-free shared latent working memory with autoregressive latent thoughts across nine benchmarks. Its broader current evidence narrows Interlat's continuing claim to its supervised last-state channel, compression objective, and controlled ALFWorld study rather than pure latent collaboration generally.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Interlat is presented as a feasibility study of communication entirely in latent space: agents transmit token-aligned last hidden states, heterogeneous actors learn to use them, and a separate latent recurrence compresses messages to as few as eight steps with up to 24x faster generation.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper supplies matched text/no-communication controls, message perturbations, actor and compressor ablations, three model backbones, two tasks, compression sweeps, and limited three-agent topologies. Official prior records already include output-embedding debate, direct activation fusion, hybrid state-delta trajectories, KV-cache fusion, and identifiable thought communication; a subsequent current method also performs training-free pure latent collaboration across more benchmarks.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest specific novelty is the supervised combination of a full token-aligned last-state channel, a token-to-latent receiver curriculum, and frozen-actor behavioral compression into a latent-only recurrence. It is not the first communication beyond text, and 'entirely latent' applies cleanly only to the compressed sender loop. Claims of genuine understanding, shared model-agnostic semantics, information preservation, and parallel hypotheses are suggestive rather than identified by the reported probes.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text pass covered all 24 pages of arXiv:2511.09149v5, including the main objectives, Tables 1-5, Equations in Sections 3-4, limitations/ethics, Appendix B's complete compression derivation, Appendix D ablations, Appendix E Tables 7-8, Appendix F probability analyses, Appendix G PCA/Table 9, and training examples. PDF/text hashes and 24/24 page coverage were recomputed locally and match the fulltext index. Six current competitor records were checked on official arXiv pages on 2026-08-23, with the post-submission LatentMAS record labeled as subsequent. Findings explicitly separate author results from equation, causal, latency, and confound audits. This is not a secondary verified review.
